Latin word

nimium

nimium, nimiī n.

noun, second declension · Declension on Wiktionary

too much, excess; too, too much

In this lexicon

  • excess

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Off. 1.89: mediocritātem illam tenēbit, quae est inter nimium et parum (Lewis & Short, s.v. nimius); Plin. NH 33 prooem. 5 (Lewis & Short)

  • too

    also used · classical · Cic. Cat. 1.10: nimium diū (Lewis & Short); Cic. Fam. 16.18.3: nimium est aquae; Traupman 88: too soon, nimium citō

  • Nē nimium.: nothing in excess

    modern

Examples

  • apprīmē in vītā esse ūtile ut nē quid nimis

    that the most useful thing in life is nothing in excessTer. And. 61

    In the entry for excess

  • mediocritātem illam tenēbit, quae est inter nimium et parum

    he will keep to that mean which lies between too much and too littleCic. Off. 1.89 (Lewis & Short)

    In the entry for excess

  • nunc quidem etiam nimium est aquae

    just now there’s even too much waterCic. Fam. 16.18.3

    In the entry for too

  • malōs cavēte; nūllī nimium crēdite

    beware of the wicked; trust no one too muchPhaedr. App. 8.15
